Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of applicant, is taken on record.
Heard Mr. Sanjeev Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Mr. Varun Singh, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of applicant, Net Singh with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No. 13 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, Police Station Awagarh, District Etah, during pendency of trial.
On 07.03.2024, the following order was passed:-
"Supplementary Affidavit, filed today, on behalf of the applicant and counter affidavit on behalf of the informant, are taken on record.

sentences.text:
On 22.02.2024 this Court has passed the following order:
"Heard Mr. Sanjeev Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned AGA for the State.
As per the allegations in the FIR, the applicant has purchased a harvester on loan and without paying the loan amount and forging NOC, the aforesaid harvester has been sold by the applicant.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant, Net Singh with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.13 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467,
468 and 471 I.P.C., Police Station Awagarh, District Etah, during pendency of trial.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further submits that the applicant is ready and willing to pay the loan dues which according to him is about Rs.5,50,000/- in easy installments.

He further submits that the loan was taken by the applicant,
however, the son of the applicant has also been falsely implicated in the present case.

He further submits that the applicant is ready and willing to deposit an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- before the CJM concerned before 28.02.2024 and the same shall be released in favour of the informant after proper verification.
In view of the above, the applicant is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the CJM concerned before 28.02.2024.
The amount so deposited shall be released in favour of the informant after proper verification.
Put up this case, as fresh on 28.02.2024.
By the said date, learned counsel for the applicant shall file an affidavit with respect to the deposition of the amount, as undertaken above."
In compliance of the aforesaid order, the applicant has deposited Rs. 1 Lakh before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Etah, as is evident from Page-5 of the Supplementary Affidavit.
Today, Mr. Varun Singh, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the informant disputed the loan dues, stating it to be Rs. 12.50 Lakh.
However, while the the case was heard on 22.02.2024, learned Counsel for the applicant informed it to be Rs. 5,50,000/-.

On the aforesaid objection raised by learned counsel for the informant, learned counsel appearing for the applicant submits that to show his bonafide the applicant is ready and willing to deposit further Rs. 2 Lakh by 12.03.2024.

As undertaken aforesaid, the applicant is permitted to deposit Rs. 2 Lakh before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Etah on or before 12.03.2024, who shall release the said amount in informant Net Singh vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9944289/
2 Company's account after proper verification.

sentences.text: Put up this case on 14th March, 2024, as fresh, showing the name of Sri Varun Singh as counsel for opposite party.
On the said date, learned counsel for the applicant shall also file an affidavit regarding the deposit of aforementioned amount.
Office to issue certified copy of this order to learned counsel for the applicant today itself."

After hearing counsel for the parties, the Court had directed the applicant to deposit Rs. Two Lacs before Chief Judicial Magistrate, Etah on or before 12.03.2024, who shall release the said amount in informant Company's account after proper verification.

In compliance of the aforesaid orders, the applicant has deposited Rs. One Lakh on 27.02.2023 and Rs. Two Lakh on 11.03.2024 before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Etah, receipts of the same have been annexed alongwith Supplementary Affidavit.

The aforesaid amount will be given to the informant Company's account after proper verification and rest of the amount of Rs. Two and a half Lakh shall be deposited within two months after being released and the said amount will also be given to the informant Company's account after proper verification.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that in paragraph 24 of the bail application that applicant has no previous criminal history.
Applicant is languishing in jail since 12.12.2023.

In case,
he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the trial by all means and there is no chance of applicant fleeing away from judicial process or tampering with the witnesses.
Per contra learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant.
Mr. Varun Singh, learned counsel for the informant disputed the loan dues, stating it to be Rs. 12.50 Lakh till January, 2023.

However, while the the case was heard on 22.02.2024,
learned Counsel for the applicant informed it to be Rs. 5,50,000/-.
The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because he or she is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Apex Court in Satyendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51.

sentences.text: The object of the bail is to secure the attendance of the accused, the detention of the accused pending trial cannot be punitive in nature as there is presumption of innocence in favour of the accused person.
Learned A.G.A. has not brought any facts and circumstances to demonstrate that the character of the accused-applicant (s) is such that his mere presence at large would intimidate the witness.
Learned AGA for the State has not brought any fact or circumstances to indicate criminal history or antecedents of the applicant which would dis-entitle the applicant for Bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, the period of detention of the applicant for the alleged offence, submissions of learned counsel for the parties, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant involved in the aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned,
subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted and/or the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(vi) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
(vii) In the event, the applicant changes residential address, the applicant shall inform the court concerned about new residential address in writing.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
